topic: The Geometry of Light: Sphere Surface Area and Its Projected Shadow

sections.title: Prerequisite Visualization: The Circle vs. The Sphere
lecture_lines: A sphere has a constant radius from its center.
Parallel light casts a circular shadow on planes.
animations: Draw a 2D circle in light blue (#ADD8E6) centered.
Transform the circle into a 3D sphere representation.
Label the circle radius 'r' in white (#FFFFFF).
Label the sphere radius 'r' in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the cross-section of the sphere with color #FFD700.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Shadow
lecture_lines: Parallel light rays hit a sphere perfectly.
The shadow is a circle with radius r.
Its area is pi times r squared.
animations: Display a light source above a sphere.
Animate the shadow forming on a plane below.
Change the shadow color to grey (#808080) for contrast.

sections.title: Sphere Surface Area: The Archimedes Insight
lecture_lines: Surface area of a sphere is 4 pi r squared.
This is four times the shadow's area.
Visualize four shadow discs covering the sphere.
animations: Show a sphere inside a cylinder of same radius.
Fade in the surface area formula 4πr².
Compare sphere area to cylinder side area.
Flash the final equivalence relation in #FFD700.

sections.title: Synthesis and Practical Application
lecture_lines: Sphere surface is four times its shadow area.
Heat absorption depends on this total surface.
Surface area dictates energy collection capacity.
animations: Display a real-world object like a globe.
Highlight its surface using geometric projection.
Animate calculation of total surface area.

sections.title: Summary and Quick Quiz
lecture_lines: Sphere surface is 4 times shadow area.
Shadow area is pi times r squared.
Calculate surface area from shadow easily.
